picks.style: archaic greek war-chant, low drum and rasping horn over drone, harsh male voice, slow, dread-filled, hammering
picks.why: The centre of the shield: Fear worked in adamant, staring backwards with burning eyes, and the bones crumbling under parching Sirius.

picks.style: greek wedding song, aulos and lyre with tambourine, layered young voices, torchlit, dancing, joyous
picks.why: The city of gold gates on the shield — bride on the car, torches rolling in waves, pipes and lyres and 'the whole town filled with mirth'.

picks.style: greek ekphrastic hymn, lyre and light flute over shimmering percussion, clear voice, floating, marvelling
picks.why: The tin harbour that seems to heave, silver dolphins, a fisherman poised to cast — then Perseus flying with his feet touching nothing.

picks.style: roman elegy, cithara and low strings, intimate male voice, rubato, rueful, confiding
picks.why: 'Cynthia first ensnared me, wretched, with her eyes' — the opening of the whole book, and Love pressing his foot on the poet's head.

picks.style: latin pastoral lament, single flute with distant answering voices, soft tenor, watery, receding, echoing
picks.why: The nymphs pulling Hylas under, and Heracles calling three times while the breeze carries the name back from the farthest mountains.

picks.style: latin memento mori, low bowed strings and a struck bell, grave baritone, slow, processional, unadorned
picks.why: 'It is an evil, but that road must be trodden by all' — not beauty saved Nireus, nor strength Achilles, nor Croesus his gold.

picks.style: labouring song, hammered rhythm on wood over bass drone, tired baritone, plodding, circular, unrelenting
picks.why: 'Like Sisyphus, our Work is never done; continually rolls back the restless Stone' — a thresher's year closing on itself.

picks.style: threshing-floor work song, flail rhythm and fiddle, rough chorus of men, driving, bitter, call-and-response
picks.why: Men so dusted they frighten their own children, and the master counting bushels: 'Why, look ye, Rogues, d'ye think that this will do?'

picks.style: georgian horatian air, viol and recorder, calm tenor, short lines, philosophical, steady
picks.why: 'They leave their Country, not themselves, behind' — care hunting the horseman down, swifter than mountain roes.

picks.style: english ode, harpsichord and strings, clear tenor, trochaic, spectral, quickening then darkening
picks.why: 'Life, the dear precarious boon, soon we lose; alas! how soon' — the ages of a life passing as figures in a glass.

picks.style: midsummer serenade, guitar and flute, warm low voice, languid, nocturnal, amorous
picks.why: 'Come, gentle Eve, the friend of Care, come, Cynthia, lovely queen of night' — a summoning song with a roses-and-wine bower at the end of it.

picks.style: winter ode, muted strings and low woodwind, plain baritone, cold, spare, warming at the close
picks.why: 'The leafless wood, the naked field, the snow-topt cott, the frozen rill' — and then 'Haste, close the window, bar the doors.'

picks.style: english pastoral ballad, fiddle and pipe, sweet tenor, anapestic lilt, springlike, courting
picks.why: Marked A PASTORAL BALLAD and it behaves like one — dew on the buds, the cuckoo naming the season to woo, a swinging four-line stanza.

picks.style: summer pastoral air, recorder and guitar, soft paired voices, languid, shaded, drowsy
picks.why: Two shadows on the watery glass while the fish play, and the herds told to stop lowing so she can be heard.

picks.style: winter fireside ballad, hurdy-gurdy and bodhran, hearty chorus, brisk, ruddy, tale-telling
picks.why: The dairymaid thawing flakes of ice out of the cream, and the lads and lasses round the embers talking of ghosts 'till they're all in a sweat'.

picks.style: greek recitation opening into song, lyre over drone, storyteller's voice giving way to a sung priamel, measured, warming
picks.why: Carries Pindar's own beginning — 'Shall I Ismenus sing, or Melia, that from spindles all of gold her twisted yarn unwinds' — the best verse in this text.

picks.style: athenian comic chorus, aulos and hand drum, jeering massed voices with solo interjections, brisk, mocking, gossipy
picks.why: Weak field, but this one has a real chorus to sing: 'Ye heard, ye heard, my comrades, O! Our Nicias was taken in the very act!'

picks.style: enlightenment anthem, chamber organ and strings, calm solo voice opening to chorus, stately, resolving, luminous
picks.why: 'All are but parts of one stupendous whole, whose body Nature is, and God the soul' — anaphora built for a chorus, ending on 'whatever is, is right'.
